title: Prompt curation stewardship for config+model-change evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight stewardship workflow for golden promptsets tied to model and configuration changes. The goal is to ensure every model/config rollout triggers controlled regressions checks against curated promptsets, with immutable snapshots, ACLs for stewards, and an audit trail for approvals and changes. This work sits between runtime change events (model/version/dequantization flags) and the eval automation pipeline so we can reliably gate rollouts when quality regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Promptset objects can be created with metadata (owner, tags, sensitivity) and stored as immutable snapshots
A role-based ACL model exists: steward, reviewer, consumer; enforcement integrates with Console RBAC and SSO
On model/config change, the system selects relevant golden promptsets and triggers eval jobs automatically
If evals show regression beyond threshold, rollout is automatically paused and a rollback ticket is created
All promptset changes and eval decisions are recorded in an audit log with links to artifacts (PRs, diffs)

notes_and_tradeoffs: Option A: Store promptset blobs in Catalog DB as compressed JSON. Pros: single-system queries. Cons: DB bloat and slower snapshotting. Current decision: use S3 blobs + lightweight DB metadata record.
We debated strict immutability vs. append-only updates. Chosen pattern: immutable snapshot per change + a mutable 'current pointer' for consumer convenience.
Decision to gate rollouts automatically on regression detects requires careful threshold tuning; initial thresholds will be conservative and surfaced to PMs for adjustment.
Also considering 'signed snapshots' to make tamper evidence explicit for regulated customers; may add HMAC signatures in a follow-up.

Performance note: running full golden evals on every minor config change is expensive. Plan: run full evals for model version changes and a trimmed smoke suite for config toggles, with a configurable escalation policy.
